public_rationale: The filing supplies material evidence against a simple proportional relationship: Anthropic's operating expenses declined sharply relative to revenue through June. But most of that series predates the post, and its final quarter is the discounted quarter Zitron expressly discussed. It does not establish the sustained post-publication change required for early resolution. The claim also leaves its cost measure and accounting basis unspecified. No decisive event satisfying the contract is established by the evaluation date.
limitations: The result depends on reading linearly as a persistent economic relationship rather than an exact equality.
The available filing covers one lab and ends in June 2026.
Operating expenses, computing expenditure, adjusted profit and net income are different measures.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI labs' costs rise linearly with revenue and will keep doing so indefinitely.

statement.excerpt: Costs increase linearly with revenue, and will continue to do so in perpetuity.

our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion concerns frontier AI labs, especially Anthropic and OpenAI.
An ordinary reading is that business costs will keep rising roughly in proportion to realized revenue, preventing sustained improvement in the cost-to-revenue ratio.
I do not interpret linearly as an exact mathematical equality in every reporting period.
Costs are not defined as inference costs, total operating expenses, cash spending or all expenses. No accounting basis is specified.
Because the post explicitly discusses a temporarily discounted quarter, one quarter of improved margins alone does not meet the early-resolution rule.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable observations can support the relationship over a finite period, but cannot establish that it will persist forever.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A consistent financial series for a lab within scope establishes a sustained material departure from proportional cost growth after publication, with the change surviving adjustments for temporary discounts, expense timing and accounting changes.

evidence.locator: Quarterly Results of Operations, introductory paragraph and Quarterly Consolidated Statements of Operations table
evidence.publisher: Anthropic, PBC / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
evidence.explanation: The table shows total operating expenses falling from approximately 239% of revenue in Q4 2025 to 135% in Q1 2026 and 92% in Q2 2026, material countercontext to proportional growth. Only the final quarter overlaps the forecast, and the defined GAAP operating-expense measure cannot be silently substituted for the claim's unspecified costs.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A clarified cost definition and accounting basis, followed by comparable disclosures showing a sustained post-publication departure from proportional growth beyond temporary supplier terms. Continuing proportional growth would support only the observed period, not perpetuity.
